about.en: A cross grip puts your partner's arm diagonally across their own body, and a straight crossing arm is a lever. Bringing your elbow over it and pinning it to your chest breaks the angle, and turning your shoulder in does the same; either leaves their arm across their body and your throw towards it.

en: Elbow over the crossing arm, then pin it to your chest
Or turn your gripped shoulder in and their angle is gone
The trapped arm is the one you throw on
Lift the elbow on the gripped side over your partner's crossing arm.
Drop the elbow and pin their arm against your chest.
Or turn the gripped shoulder in towards them so their grip loses its angle.
Attack on the arm you have trapped.

receiving.en: Their elbow coming over your crossing arm and dropping onto it pins your arm across your own chest. Let go before it is pinned and re-grip on the near side.

viNotes.en: You can feel the diagonal of their arm across your chest; the elbow goes over it at the point nearest your shoulder. Once pinned, their arm is under your hand and the throw is on that side.
